À remplacer mot pour mot par les textes publiés (« In order to accomplish the aim of the preceding paragraph » est la formule usuelle de l'art. 9 al. 2 mais n'a pas été revérifiée).
Le repère est une phrase de la fiche, traduite fidèlement ; la source (NDL) est en anglais, l'adresse reste la même.

titre: Japan's 1946 Constitution, Written by GHQ, Adopted as an Amendment
accroche: Drafted within GHQ between February 4 and 12, 1946, the draft is adopted by the Diet under the 1889 amendment procedure.
contenu_vulgarise:
## A draft judged unacceptable

On February 1, 1946, the newspaper Mainichi calls “too conservative” the draft of the committee led by Joji Matsumoto, tasked by the Japanese government with revising the 1889 Constitution. The Allied headquarters (GHQ) draws an argument from this: as long as the Far Eastern Commission has not set a policy, nothing binds it on constitutional matters. On February 3, General MacArthur hands Courtney Whitney, head of GHQ's Government Section, the requirements for constitutional reform, the “MacArthur Notes.” A team from the Government Section gets to work on the 4th. Matsumoto sends in his own plan on the 8th.

On the evening of the 10th, the Government Section's draft is submitted to MacArthur, who approves it while demanding the removal of a clause forbidding any future revision from limiting the guaranteed liberties. The text is completed on the 12th. On February 13, Whitney tells Matsumoto and Foreign Minister Shigeru Yoshida that their proposal is “totally unacceptable” and hands them the GHQ draft. On the 22nd, the Japanese cabinet decides to accept GHQ's constitutional reform policy. On March 6, it presents an “outline of a draft revised constitution.”

## A procedure from 1889

A text drafted by the occupier could have been proclaimed by the occupier. That is not the path chosen. The draft is presented as an amendment to the 1889 Constitution of the Empire of Japan, Article 73 of which provides that a draft amendment is submitted to the Diet by imperial order, and that neither house may adopt it without a majority of two-thirds of the members present. The Diet was elected on April 10, 1946, in the first election in which women vote. An imperial rescript of June 20 sends the “draft revision of the Imperial Constitution” to both houses.

The deputies do not merely register it. A subcommittee of the House of Representatives, within the committee chaired by Hitoshi Ashida, sits behind closed doors from July 25 to August 20 and adds to the beginning of the second paragraph of Article 9 the words “in order to accomplish the aim of the preceding paragraph.” The House of Peers has a “civilian clause” added, at GHQ's request. The representatives vote the text on August 24 by 421 votes to 8. The peers approve it on October 6, the representatives confirm it on the 7th with five votes against, and the Privy Council gives its assent on October 29.

## Neither imposed, nor freely chosen

The text is promulgated on November 3, 1946, and takes effect on May 3, 1947. Before it was sent to the Diet, the Privy Council had already approved the draft by an overwhelming majority, with only one of its members opposed: Tatsukichi Minobe.

This chronology undoes the convenient alternative between an “imposed” constitution and a “Japanese” one. The text's origin is American, and the Tokyo government first proposed something entirely different. But its formal validity comes from a rule of the regime it replaces: the 1889 Constitution supplied the path by which it ceased to exist. What remains is to know what a regular procedure is worth when the idea comes from elsewhere: the dates establish the facts; they do not settle that question.

repere.texte: On August 24, 1946, the Japanese House of Representatives adopts the draft revision of the Constitution by 421 votes to 8. On October 7, after the House of Peers' amendments, it confirms it with five votes against.
repere.source: National Diet Library, “The Birth of the Constitution of Japan,” commentary “Deliberations in the Imperial Diet”

carte.punch: Written at MacArthur's headquarters, Japan's Constitution is voted as an amendment.
carte.idee: Between February 4 and 12, 1946, GHQ's Government Section drafts a constitution. It nonetheless goes before the Diet through Article 73 of the 1889 Constitution: 421 votes to 8 in the House of Representatives, on August 24, 1946.

quiz.question: What does recourse to Article 73 of the 1889 Constitution change for the text drafted by GHQ?
choix: The text is proclaimed by MacArthur, the Diet being consulted only symbolically
The text is submitted to a national referendum, as that article provided
The text follows the 1889 revision path and the Diet votes it, which ensures legal continuity
The emperor declines to promulgate the text, that role being given to the Allied commander
quiz.explication: Article 73 provides for sending a draft to the Diet by imperial order and a vote by a two-thirds majority. The Diet amended and voted the text (421 votes to 8 on August 24, 1946), there was no referendum, and promulgation took place on November 3, 1946 as an imperial assent, not by MacArthur.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the subcommittee led by Hitoshi Ashida add to the second paragraph of Article 9?
choix: A clause excluding women from the right to vote for the Diet
A clause reserving ministerial posts for civilians
The words “in order to accomplish the aim of the preceding paragraph,” at the beginning of the paragraph
The removal of the clause forbidding future revisions from limiting the guaranteed liberties
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Ashida subcommittee sits behind closed doors from July 25 to August 20, 1946, and adds those words at the beginning of the second paragraph of Article 9; the civilian clause comes from the House of Peers, at GHQ's request.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the emperor do on June 20, 1946, after the Diet's election?
choix: He promulgates the new Constitution before the assembled Diet
He sends the draft revision by rescript to both houses of the Diet
He dissolves the Diet elected in April in order to call another
He personally approves the text before it is handed to the cabinet
quiz_supplementaire.explication: An imperial rescript of June 20, 1946 sends the draft revision of the Imperial Constitution to both houses of the Diet, elected the previous April 10.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Who, in the Privy Council, is the only one to oppose the draft constitutional revision?
choix: Joji Matsumoto, head of the revision committee
Courtney Whitney, head of the Government Section
Tatsukichi Minobe, the lone opponent on the Privy Council
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Privy Council approves the draft on October 29, 1946 by an overwhelming majority, Tatsukichi Minobe being the only one of its members to oppose it.
